findings.title: `renderValue`'s separator JSDoc claims the two control characters "cannot occur in a catalogue name or definition"; U+0001 can appear in a PostgreSQL text comment, so two different comment lists can in principle render equal.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: U+0000 genuinely cannot appear in a PostgreSQL text value, so the FIELD separator is safe; U+0001 is an ordinary text character and `columnComments` / the table `comment` carry arbitrary text. Theoretical rather than reachable in this repo — no checked-in comment contains a control character — and the equality diffs in the suites are deep-equals on structured arrays rather than on renderValue, so only `assertOnlyTablesMoved` and the vacuity check use the rendering. Recorded because it is a stated impossibility that is not impossible; fix is to narrow the claim to U+0000 or to render with a len || ROUND 2: renderEntry is JSON.stringify of the pair, injective for any string content, so there is no separator claim left to keep true. R2-M08 kills. 682d1cf34.

findings.title: Deriving the column-privilege set closed RT-7's growth blind spot and opened a shrink blind spot: narrowing deriveColumnPrivileges to SELECT alone left every caller passing.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Measured, not inferred: mutation R2-M14 SURVIVED at 4e3b756d42f4ffdcca623bfa4f83531a728af649. The mutation is semantically meaningful — every caller asserts only that the client roles hold none of whatever the function returns, so a probe returning one privilege checks one privilege, and a migration granting INSERT (actor_user_id) to anon would pass. It is not equivalent and not on an unexecuted branch. The call sites' own guard, `length > 0`, was satisfied by the mutant. Fixed in 476145667bce3e36dda6d445550f2e84fa6be096 by COLUMN_PRIVILEGE_FLOOR = 4 inside the helper, so both call sites inherit it; their local assertion is now toContain('SELECT'). Re-measured at this HEAD: killed. || ROUND 2: this is a defect the fix pass introduced while fixing RT-7, caught by the pass that exists to disprove 'done'. Recorded as deviation D16.

findings.title: rowDigest made every catalogue comparison sensitive to a concurrent committer, and the guard transactions ran at READ COMMITTED.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Found by the pre-push hook, not by this pass: the hook runs `vitest run --changed` at DEFAULT parallelism where the gate runs each live-DB file as its own serialized row, so only the hook exercises concurrency. Two cases failed that had passed three consecutive green gates. Measured cause: the container is shared and no longer empty (job_outbox 8 rows, analytics_events 20, poller_heartbeats 1 from a live judge_sweep heartbeat), and under READ COMMITTED each statement takes a fresh snapshot, so a row committed between the two catalogue readings reads as a change the migration did not make. The advisory lock serializes the nine sibling suites, not an unrelated writer. Two assertions had also been written on a zero-rows SNAPSHOT as though it were an invariant. Fixed in 87cdfb503 by ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ plus schemaOnly on 118's drop case and a count-agnostic harness assertion; proven on the live container (inside RR a concurrent COMMIT reads 1 then 1 while outside reads 2). The fix had NO covering test, which Direction B calls a P1 in its own right, so 32f4d1e2c adds one that commits from a separate connection mid-comparison. R3-M01 kills it. Recorded as deviation D17.
